## Agents

### `cortex serve`

**Answers:** Runs the MCP server on stdin and stdout so an AI agent can query
the index.

**Use it when:** An agent launches it; you rarely run it by hand.

**Run:** `cortex serve --list-tools`, then one real MCP exchange piped to
`cortex serve`: `initialize`, then `tools/call` for `find_callers` with
`{"name": "updateStatus"}`.

**Output:**

```console
$ cortex serve --list-tools
MCP profile "minimal" exposes 7 tool(s):
  get_project_overview
  search_code
  find_symbol
  get_symbol
  find_references
  find_callers
  get_task_context
```

The text of the `find_callers` tool result:

```text
=== SYSTEM METADATA ===
1 caller(s) of updateStatus (src/main/java/com/pay/service/TransactionService.java:18).
index_revision: 3  status: ready
note: 42 references repository-wide are unresolved or ambiguous, so this list may be incomplete.
provenance: This compares commits only. Staged, unstaged and untracked changes are invisible to the index and are NOT reflected here — a matching commit does not mean the working tree matches.
verdict: strong (high=1)
next_step: No result fell below high confidence. Act on these, but verify before deleting anything.

=== INFERRED ===
- calls handleCallback  src/main/java/com/pay/controller/CallbackController.java:23  [confidence=high source=source_code]  (receiver type matches)
```

On stderr at start-up:

```text
time=… level=INFO msg="serving MCP on stdio" project=payment-platform profile=minimal tools=7
```

**How to read it:**

- `--list-tools` shows what the agent will see. To add `impact_analysis` and
  `find_tests`, set `mcp.profile: standard` (or `full`) in `.cortex.yml`.
- Each tool result starts with a metadata block: the count, index revision,
  a `note` on how much is unbound, a `verdict` (strong or weak, with counts per
  confidence), and a `next_step` for the agent.
- The text is split into labelled sections. `SYSTEM METADATA` is RepoCortex's
  own report. `INFERRED` holds results it derived from the graph.
  `SOURCE EVIDENCE` holds verbatim repository content and comes with a note to
  treat it as data, not instructions. `DEVELOPER RULES` carries rules from
  the repository's configuration.
- The index does not see uncommitted edits; the metadata says so on every call.

**Useful flags:** `--list-tools`.

### `cortex agent`

**Answers:** Prints the MCP registration line and the guidance text an agent
needs, and checks what is already wired up.

**Use it when:** Connecting an agent by hand.

**Run:** `cortex agent --check`, then `cortex agent`

**Output:**

```console
$ cortex agent --check
[ok  ]  index             revision 3 — 18 files, 105 symbols, 37 relationships
[ok  ]  resolution        68% of the 31 references that name something this index defines are bound (32 matched nothing here)
[ok  ]  mcp tools         profile "minimal" exposes 7: get_project_overview, search_code, find_symbol, get_symbol, find_references, find_callers, get_task_context
                            means: impact_analysis and find_tests are not exposed on this profile; the guidance falls back to find_callers
                            do:    set mcp.profile: standard in .cortex.yml (or .cortex.yml) to add them
[warn]  mcp registration  not in this repository's .mcp.json
                            means: no project-scope registration; a user- or local-scope one is not visible from here
                            do:    cortex agent, and run the 'claude mcp add' line it prints
[warn]  guidance          not found in CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md
                            means: the agent has the tools but no rule telling it when to use them, so it will keep grepping
                            do:    cortex agent --guidance >> CLAUDE.md
[warn]  plugin manifest   .claude-plugin/plugin.json absent
                            means: this repository cannot be installed as a Claude Code plugin; the one-line registration still works
                            do:    not required — see docs/agent-integration.md
```

```console
$ cortex agent
RepoCortex agent integration for "payment-platform"

1. Register the MCP server.

   Claude Code, one line:

     claude mcp add cortex -- cortex --project /work/payment-platform serve
   …
   Any other MCP client, over stdio:

     command  cortex
     args     --project /work/payment-platform serve
     transport stdio

   Profile "minimal" exposes 7 tool(s): …

2. Give the agent the guidance below — …

     cortex agent --guidance >> CLAUDE.md

3. Confirm it landed:

     cortex agent --check

<!-- cortex:guidance -->
## RepoCortex

RepoCortex serves a resolved index of this repository over MCP. For questions
about code that already exists, prefer it to grep and to opening files.

- Before changing code, call `get_task_context` with the task in plain English.
…
<!-- /cortex:guidance -->
```

**How to read it:**

- `--check` prints one line per piece: `ok` or `warn`, then `means:` (why it
  matters) and `do:` (the exact fix). `warn` is the normal starting state, not a
  failure.
- `cortex agent` prints three numbered steps. Step 1 is the registration
  command, step 2 the guidance block (between the `cortex:guidance` markers),
  step 3 the check.
- The command changes nothing. `--write <path>` writes the guidance to a new
  file and refuses to overwrite one unless you add `--force`.

**Useful flags:** `--check`, `--guidance`, `--write <path>`, `--force`.

**Exit codes:** `--check` exits `0` unless something is actually broken.

### `cortex install`

**Answers:** Writes the MCP registration into the config of every agent client
it finds on this machine.

**Use it when:** You want one command to connect all your agents.

**Run:** `cortex install --dry-run`, and `cortex install --list` to see every supported agent

**Output:**

```console
$ cortex install --dry-run
would update  Antigravity                  ~/.gemini/config/mcp_config.json
would update  Claude Code                  ~/.claude.json
would update  Claude Desktop               ~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json
would update  Codex CLI                    ~/.codex/config.toml
would create  Copilot CLI                  ~/.copilot/mcp-config.json
would create  Cursor                       ~/.cursor/mcp.json
would create  VS Code (Copilot)            ~/Library/Application Support/Code/User/mcp.json

Nothing was written. Run without --dry-run to apply.
```

**How to read it:**

- One line per agent detected on this machine: `would update` (its config file
  exists and gains one entry), `would create` (the file is made). Without
  `--dry-run` the same lines read `updated`, `created` or `unchanged`.
- A `manual` line means the file could not be merged safely, usually JSON with
  comments. The file is left untouched and the line says what to do.
- Every other server and setting in those files is kept. Each agent gets the
  shape its own documentation specifies (`mcpServers`, `servers`,
  `context_servers`, a Codex TOML table, a Goose YAML extension, and so on).
- `cortex install --list` shows all supported agents, which are detected here,
  the exact file each one uses, and the manual step for agents that are
  configured through their own command or settings screen.
- Agents without detection are skipped; `--create` writes them anyway.

**Useful flags:** `--dry-run`, `--list`, `--create` (write configs for agents
not detected), `--rules` (add guidance to `AGENTS.md` and to any agent
instruction file the project already has).

### `cortex context`

**Answers:** Which files, symbols, tables, config and tests a plain-English
task touches, ranked and sized for an agent.

**Use it when:** Starting a task, or checking why an agent was given what it
was given.

**Run:** `cortex context "Add idempotency to payment callback processing" --show-excluded`

**Output:** (rows and the `WHY` column are shortened, so the columns were
re-aligned; every row after the first five ends with the same "source
withheld" note.)

```console
$ cortex context "Add idempotency to payment callback processing" --show-excluded
Task: Add idempotency to payment callback processing
Understood as: Concepts: callback, idempotency, payment, processing, add; action: add. Anchored on 15 symbols named by the task (PAYMENT_CALLBACK_SECRET, services.payments.environment.PAYMENT_CALLBACK_SECRET, POST /payment/callback, payment.callback, payment.callback.secret, …); expanded to 42 reachable symbols in the call graph

KIND             NAME                     LOCATION                                                        WHY
class            CallbackController       src/main/java/com/pay/controller/CallbackController.java:11     named by the task (matches "callback" and "payment"); relevant members: CallbackController, POST /payment/callback, handleCallback, +1 more; …
configuration    PAYMENT_CALLBACK_SECRET  Dockerfile:4                                                    named by the task (matches "callback" and "payment")
…
test             CallbackControllerTest   src/test/java/com/pay/controller/CallbackControllerTest.java:3  named by the task (matches "callback"); …
class            TransactionService       src/main/java/com/pay/service/TransactionService.java:6         1 hop from what the task names, through the call graph (path confidence high); relevant members: updateStatus, isDuplicate, notificationService, +2 more; …
test             TransactionServiceTest   src/test/java/com/pay/service/TransactionServiceTest.java:3     regression coverage for TransactionService, matched by test naming convention — no call edge between them was resolved; …
class            TransactionRepository    src/main/java/com/pay/repository/TransactionRepository.java:3   2 hops from what the task names, through the call graph (path confidence high); relevant members: findById, save, jdbc; writes transaction_events, writes transactions; …
table            transactions             src/main/resources/db/migration/V1__create_transactions.sql:1   persistence touched by TransactionRepository (writes); …
table            transaction_events       src/main/resources/db/migration/V1__create_transactions.sql:13  persistence touched by TransactionRepository (writes); …
class            NotificationService      src/main/java/com/pay/notification/NotificationService.java:3   2 hops from what the task names, through the call graph (path confidence high); relevant members: send, client; …
…

26 item(s), roughly 2741 tokens.

Graph expansion was bounded: depth limit 3 reached, and 8 node(s) at the limit were not expanded. Symbols beyond that boundary are not represented in this pack.

Source was allocated by relevance, not evenly: 1 item of 26 items carry an excerpt inside a ~1920-character source budget, and 21 items named without it. Each of those says why in its own reason; the paths and lines above fetch the rest.

Excluded (1):
  MarketingReport  matches "payment" textually (only 1 task term; 2 terms required without a structural connection), but no dependency path connects it to anything the task names, it covers no included code, and it shares no table with the flow
```

**How to read it:**

- **Understood as** shows the words it took from the task and the symbols it
  started from. If the starting symbols are wrong, reword the task with real
  names.
- **Each row** is one item. `WHY` says how it earned its place: `named by the
  task` (word match), `N hops … through the call graph` (followed from a named
  item, with the path's confidence), `persistence touched by …` (a table), or a
  test matched by naming convention.
- The order is the ranking. The top items are the ones to read first.
- **Footer.** Item count and token estimate; whether graph expansion hit its
  depth limit; how the source budget was split.
- **Excluded** (with `--show-excluded`) lists what was considered and dropped,
  with the reason. Here the unrelated marketing class was dropped correctly.
- Config keys that share a task word (`payment.*`) can crowd out code. Use
  `--max-symbols` or a more specific task.

**Useful flags:** `--show-excluded`, `--max-files N`, `--max-symbols N`,
`--max-lines N`.

### `cortex compile`

**Answers:** Turns a one-line request into a task contract: scope, out of
scope, constraints, risks and unknowns, each with evidence.

**Use it when:** Before handing a task to an agent, and to produce the input
for `verify`.

**Run:** `cortex compile "Add idempotency to payment callback processing"`

**Output:** (long `source withheld` notes are cut with `…`.)

```console
$ cortex compile "Add idempotency to payment callback processing"
# Task Contract

## Intent

Add idempotency to payment callback processing

## Interpretation

Concepts: callback, idempotency, payment, processing, add; action: add. Anchored on 15 symbols named by the task (…); expanded to 42 reachable symbols in the call graph

## Goal

Add idempotency to payment callback processing.

## Scope

- `CallbackController` in `src/main/java/com/pay/controller/CallbackController.java` (class) — named by the task (matches "callback" and "payment"); …
- `PAYMENT_CALLBACK_SECRET` in `Dockerfile` (configuration) — named by the task (matches "callback" and "payment")
…
- `payment.notify` in `src/main/resources/application.yml` (configuration) — named by the task (matches "payment"); …

## Out of scope

- `MarketingReport` in `unrelated/marketing/MarketingReport.java` — matches "payment" textually (…), but no dependency path connects it to anything the task names, …

## Constraints

- Behaviour here is configuration-driven; a new setting needs a default that preserves the current behaviour of deployments that do not set it.
  - evidence: PAYMENT_CALLBACK_SECRET (Dockerfile), PAYMENT_CALLBACK_SECRET (docker-compose.yml), payment (src/main/resources/application.yml) and 6 more
- Declared architecture rule "controllers-do-not-touch-the-database": controller must not depend on repository. Controllers must go through a service.
  - evidence: architecture rule controllers-do-not-touch-the-database (severity high) in the declared component model; scope in component controller; CallbackController (src/main/java/com/pay/controller/CallbackController.java)

## Acceptance

- [ ] Every entry under Scope is either changed, or left unchanged for a stated reason.
- [ ] No file outside Scope is modified without saying why it had to be.

## Risks

- **medium** The scope is wide enough that a change applied in one place and forgotten in another is the likely failure; work through the scope list explicitly rather than from memory.
  - evidence: 12 scope entries across 6 file(s)

## Unknowns

- The impact analysis could not resolve "CallbackController" in the index, …
- The analysis found no test covering the scope symbols it examined, …
- Scope was capped at 12 entries and 14 further ranked candidate(s) were dropped; if the work turns out to reach past this list, the cap hid where.
…
```

**How to read it:**

- **Scope** is what the change may touch. **Out of scope** is what it must not
  touch; `verify` treats an edit there as a fact.
- **Constraints** come from declared rules, config and code, each with an
  `evidence` line. No evidence, no constraint.
- **Risks** are graded and cited.
- **Unknowns** are the gaps. Read them. Here the scope cap pushed
  `TransactionService` out of the 12-entry scope in favour of config keys, so a
  change there will show as "neither in scope nor out of scope" in `verify`.
  Raise `--max-scope` when that happens.
- Save it with `cortex --json compile "…" > contract.json` for `verify`.

**Useful flags:** `--max-scope N`.

### `cortex verify`

**Answers:** Did a change stay inside its task contract, respect the declared
rules, reach every flagged caller, and keep its tests?

**Use it when:** After an agent or a person finishes a task, and in CI.

**Run:**

```console
$ cortex --json compile "Add idempotency to payment callback processing" > contract.json
$ cortex verify --contract contract.json --changed src/main/java/com/pay/service/TransactionService.java
VERIFY: ADVISORY

[LEAD] src/main/java/com/pay/service/TransactionService.java violates architecture rule services-do-not-notify-directly: updateStatus (service) calls send (notification).
  evidence: src/main/java/com/pay/service/TransactionService.java:25 — updateStatus CALLS send, high confidence; rule services-do-not-notify-directly, verdict forbidden
  receiver type matches

UNKNOWN
  1 changed file(s) appear in neither Scope nor Out of scope; the contract took no position on them, so this check has nothing to say about whether they belonged in the change.
  The contract carries no blast radius, so this check cannot say whether a caller was missed. Compile with an impact source to make this question answerable.
```

Adding an edit to an out-of-scope file:

```console
$ cortex verify --contract contract.json --changed src/main/java/com/pay/service/TransactionService.java,unrelated/marketing/MarketingReport.java
VERIFY: FAIL

[FACT] unrelated/marketing/MarketingReport.java was edited, and the contract listed it as out of scope.
  evidence: contract out-of-scope entry for MarketingReport (unrelated/marketing/MarketingReport.java)
  matches "payment" textually (…)
[LEAD] src/main/java/com/pay/service/TransactionService.java violates architecture rule services-do-not-notify-directly: …
…
```

**How to read it:**

- First line is the verdict: `PASS`, `ADVISORY` (only leads), `FAIL` (at least
  one fact) or `UNVERIFIED` (nothing to check against).
- `[FACT]` rests on something certain: the contract itself or an `exact` edge.
  Act on it.
- `[LEAD]` rests on a `high`, `medium` or `low` edge. Confirm it by reading the
  evidence line.
- `UNKNOWN` lists questions the check could not answer, and why.

**Useful flags:** `--contract` (required), `--changed a,b,c` or
`--changed-from file` (`-` for stdin), `--fail-on-leads`, `--min-confidence`.

**Exit codes:** `0` pass or advisory; `1` fail; `2` unverified. With
`--fail-on-leads`, advisory also exits non-zero.

### `cortex prune`

**Answers:** The file with method bodies removed, keeping signatures, types and
doc comments.

**Use it when:** Giving an agent the shape of a large file without its bodies.

**Run:** `cortex prune src/main/java/com/pay/service/TransactionService.java`

**Output:**

```console
$ cortex prune src/main/java/com/pay/service/TransactionService.java
package com.pay.service;

import com.pay.repository.TransactionRepository;
import com.pay.notification.NotificationService;

@Service
public class TransactionService {

    private final TransactionRepository repository;
    private final NotificationService notificationService;

    public TransactionService(TransactionRepository repository,
                              NotificationService notificationService) { /* ... */ }

    public void updateStatus(String transactionId, String status) { /* ... */ }

    private boolean isDuplicate(Transaction txn, String status) { /* ... */ }

    public Transaction findTransaction(String transactionId) { /* ... */ }
}
```

**How to read it:**

- Everything outside function bodies is kept as written. Each body becomes the
  placeholder.
- It reads the file from disk, not the index, so it works on uncommitted edits.

**Useful flags:** `--placeholder "<text>"`, `--no-docstrings`.

### `cortex diff-minimize`

**Answers:** A shorter version of a unified diff, with the enclosing scope of
each hunk and long unchanged runs collapsed.

**Use it when:** Passing a diff to an agent with a tight token budget.

**Run:** `git diff HEAD~1 > change.diff && cortex diff-minimize change.diff`

**Output:**

```console
$ cortex diff-minimize ../change.diff
Compressed diff: 911 -> 561 bytes (38.4% token reduction, ~141 tokens)

--- src/main/java/com/pay/service/TransactionService.java (+7 -0) ---
@@ public class TransactionService { @@
 
... (1 unchanged lines) ...
         Transaction txn = repository.findById(transactionId);
+        if (isDuplicate(txn, status)) {
+            return;
+        }
         txn.setStatus(status);
... (3 unchanged lines) ...
 
+    private boolean isDuplicate(Transaction txn, String status) {
+        return status.equals(txn.getStatus());
+    }
+
     public Transaction findTransaction(String transactionId) {
... (1 unchanged lines) ...
     }
```

**How to read it:**

- The header gives sizes before and after, and an approximate token count.
- One block per file with `(+added -removed)`. The `@@ … @@` line names the
  enclosing class or function.
- `... (N unchanged lines) ...` replaces context the agent does not need.
- It also reads stdin: `git diff | cortex diff-minimize`.

## Reports and export

### `cortex report`

**Answers:** Turns the `--json` output of `impact`, `arch` and `missed` into a
pull-request comment (`report pr`) or a SARIF file (`report sarif`).

**Use it when:** In CI, to post results on a PR or to a code-scanning view.

**Run:**

```console
$ cortex --json arch   > arch.json
$ cortex --json missed > missed.json
$ cortex --json impact --base HEAD~1 --head HEAD > impact.json
$ cortex report pr --impact impact.json --arch arch.json --missed missed.json
```

**Output:**

```markdown
<!-- cortex:pr-report -->
## RepoCortex change-safety report

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Blast radius | **moderate** risk (score 45): 1 symbols reached from 7 changed symbols; 0% exact, 100% high, 0% medium |
| Architecture | 1 rule violations, 0 data-rule violations, worst medium |
| Blindspots | 43 (1 high) |

### How much of the blast radius is proven

| Confidence | Symbols | Share |
|---|---|---|
| exact (compiler-proven) | 0 | 0% |
| high | 1 | 100% |
| medium | 0 | 0% |
…
### Blast radius

| Symbol | File | Depth | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| handleCallback | src/main/java/com/pay/controller/CallbackController.java | 1 | high |

#### Could not determine

- **unresolved\_references**: 42 reference\(s\) in this run were never bound to a definition: …

### Architecture

| Rule | Severity | From → To | Location | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| services-do-not-notify-directly | medium | service → notification | src/main/java/com/pay/service/TransactionService.java:25 | high |

### Blindspots

| Severity | Kind | Target | Location |
|---|---|---|---|
| medium | unresolved\_call | request | src/main/java/com/pay/controller/CallbackController.java:23 |
…
_…and 23 more._
```

```console
$ cortex report sarif --arch arch.json --missed missed.json --out cortex.sarif
```

The SARIF file holds one run with rules such as
`cortex/arch/services-do-not-notify-directly`,
`cortex/blindspot/missing_config` and `cortex/blindspot/unresolved_call`, and
one result per finding (44 here).

**How to read it:**

- The first line, `<!-- cortex:pr-report -->`, is a marker so CI can update the
  same comment instead of posting a new one.
- The summary table has one row per input. An input you did not pass shows as
  "not run", never as zero.
- "How much of the blast radius is proven" is the share of reached symbols at
  each confidence. 0% `exact` means nothing in it was checked by a compiler.
- Tables are capped at `--max-rows`; the rest are counted.
- In SARIF, architecture violations and blindspots become code-scanning
  alerts. `--path-prefix` fixes paths when the index was built from a
  subdirectory.

**Useful flags:** `pr --out comment.md`, `pr --max-rows N`,
`sarif --out file`, `sarif --path-prefix <dir>`.

### `cortex docs`

**Answers:** Writes `ARCHITECTURE.md` and `CAPABILITIES.md` from the index,
with Mermaid diagrams and a citation for every claim.

**Use it when:** You want architecture docs that stay true, checked in CI.

**Run:** `cortex docs` (prints to stdout)

**Output:**

````markdown
# Architecture

Derived from the RepoCortex index. Every node and every arrow below is a fact recorded by an indexer, and every one cites the file and line it came from — nothing here is prose about the code.
…
Index run 3: 18 files, 105 symbols, 37 edges — of which 1 EXPOSES, 3 table read/write, 0 IMPLEMENTS/EXTENDS. 1 endpoints and 2 tables are declared.

## Components

The repository declares 4 components and 2 rules in `.cortex.yml`.

| Component | Files | Symbols | Declared include patterns |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| service | 1 | 7 | src/main/java/com/pay/service/** |
| controller | 1 | 5 | src/main/java/com/pay/controller/** |
| repository | 1 | 5 | src/main/java/com/pay/repository/** |
| notification | 1 | 4 | src/main/java/com/pay/notification/** |
…
```mermaid
graph LR
  c_service["service (1 file, 7 symbols)"]
  c_controller["controller (1 file, 5 symbols)"]
  c_repository["repository (1 file, 5 symbols)"]
  c_notification["notification (1 file, 4 symbols)"]
  c_service -.->|"1 x CALLS — violates services-do-not-notify-directly"| c_notification
  c_service -->|"3 x CALLS"| c_repository
  c_controller -->|"1 x CALLS"| c_service
```
…
## Endpoint flows
…
### POST /payment/callback
…
## Inheritance
…
This index contains no IMPLEMENTS or EXTENDS edges. …

---

Nothing was omitted: every section fitted inside its cap.
# Candidate business capabilities
…
| Capability | Endpoints | Tables | Depends on | Files | Symbols |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| controller | 1 | 0 | 1 | 1 | 5 |
| repository | 0 | 2 | 0 | 1 | 5 |
| service | 0 | 0 | 2 | 1 | 7 |
| notification | 0 | 0 | 0 | 1 | 4 |
…
````

**How to read it:**

- **Components** come from `.cortex.yml`. A component with 0 files has wrong
  globs.
- **Component dependencies**: dashed arrows violate a rule. The evidence table
  under it cites one line per dependency.
- **Endpoint flows**: one diagram per route, from route to handler to calls to
  tables, up to a fixed depth. A `Bounded:` note says what was cut.
- **Inheritance**: empty without a compiler index or a typed language that
  records `IMPLEMENTS`/`EXTENDS`.
- The last line of `ARCHITECTURE.md` says whether any section was cut.
- **CAPABILITIES.md** groups the same facts by component: endpoints, tables,
  dependencies.
- Output is byte-for-byte repeatable, so you can commit it.

**Useful flags:** `--out <dir>`, `--check` (compare with the files in `--out`),
`--max-endpoints N`, `--max-depth N`.

**Exit codes:** with `--check`, non-zero when the committed files have drifted.

### `cortex export`

**Answers:** Writes the graph in DOT, GraphML, JSON, CSV or SVG.

**Use it when:** You want to draw, query or diff the graph in another tool.

**Run:** `cortex export --format csv`, `--format dot --min-confidence high`, `--format json`

**Output:**

```console
$ cortex export --format csv
source,target,kind,confidence
event:kafka:payment.status-changed,src/main/java/com/pay/events/PaymentEventPublisher.java:kafkaTemplate,CALLS,high
src/main/java/com/pay/controller/CallbackController.java#POST /payment/callback,src/main/java/com/pay/controller/CallbackController.java:handleCallback,EXPOSES,high
src/main/java/com/pay/controller/CallbackController.java:handleCallback,src/main/java/com/pay/service/TransactionService.java:updateStatus,CALLS,high
src/main/java/com/pay/events/AuditListener.java:onStatusChanged,event:kafka:payment.status-changed,CONSUMES,high
src/main/java/com/pay/events/PaymentEventPublisher.java:statusChanged,event:kafka:payment.status-changed,PUBLISHES,high
…
src/main/java/com/pay/repository/TransactionRepository.java:save,table:transactions,WRITES,high
…
unit:docker-compose.yml#payments,src/main/java/com/pay/controller/CallbackController.java#POST /payment/callback,CONTAINS,medium
unit:docker-compose.yml#payments,unit:docker-compose.yml#db,DEPENDS_ON,high
```

On stderr:

```text
index_revision: 3  built at commit eae0f8a
note: 12 symbol(s) share a fully-qualified name with another; their node ids carry a '@<path>' (and, if that still ties, '#L<line>') suffix so no symbol is dropped and no edge is re-parented
note: csv export is lossy — edge list only: nodes with no edges are omitted, node kind is not carried, edge weight is not carried, and a cell starting with =, +, -, or @ is prefixed with a quote to block spreadsheet formula injection
```

```console
$ cortex export --format dot --min-confidence high
digraph cortex {
  graph [rankdir=LR];
  node [shape=box, fontname="Helvetica"];
  "config:PAYMENT_CALLBACK_SECRET@Dockerfile" [kind="configuration"];
  …
  "src/main/java/com/pay/controller/CallbackController.java:handleCallback" [kind="method"];
  …
```

The JSON form has `"directed": true`, a `nodes` array (`id`, `kind`) and an
`edges` array (`source`, `target`, `kind`, `confidence`, `weight`).

**How to read it:**

- Node ids: `path:Name` for code, `table:<name>`, `config:<key>`,
  `event:<broker>:<topic>`, `unit:<file>#<service>`, `dep:<coordinate>`. A
  `@<path>` or `#L<line>` suffix separates symbols that share a name.
- Edge kinds include `CALLS`, `EXPOSES`, `READS`, `WRITES`, `PUBLISHES`,
  `CONSUMES`, `CONFIGURED_BY`, `CONTAINS`, `DEPENDS_ON`.
- Notes on stderr say what the chosen format cannot hold, and how many edges
  were dropped by `--min-confidence`. Stdout stays clean for pipes.
- Render DOT with `cortex export --format dot | dot -Tsvg -o graph.svg`, or use
  `--format svg` with no Graphviz.

**Useful flags:** `--format csv|dot|graphml|json|svg`, `--out <file>`,
`--min-confidence`.

---

## Portal

### `cortex ui`

**Answers:** Serves a local, read-only web portal over the index.

**Use it when:** You want to browse the map, blast radius, tables, config,
architecture and accuracy screens instead of reading terminal output.

**Run:** `cortex ui --print-url`, then `cortex ui --port 7791`

**Output:**

```console
$ cortex ui --print-url
http://127.0.0.1:7777/

$ cortex ui --port 7791
RepoCortex portal: http://127.0.0.1:7791/
  index      /work/payment-platform/.cortex/index.db (opened read-only; this portal never writes)
  binding    loopback only — not reachable from other machines.
             Requests whose Host header is not a loopback address are refused, so a
             page on the internet cannot use your browser to read this index.

Press Ctrl-C to stop.
```

**How to read it:**

- Open the URL. The first screen is index health; read it before anything else.
- `binding loopback only` is the safe default. A request with a non-loopback
  `Host` header gets `403`.
- In the graphs, solid lines with a tick are `exact`, dashed lines are weaker,
  and the weakest are hidden by default with a count of what was hidden.

**Useful flags:** `--port N` (`0` picks a free port), `--print-url`,
`--allow-refresh` (adds one button that rebuilds the index), `--host`
(binding elsewhere exposes your code structure to the network), `--max-nodes N`.

## Housekeeping

### `cortex version`

**Answers:** Which build is this?

**Use it when:** Reporting a bug, or comparing CI and local builds.

```console
$ cortex version
cortex dev (commit none, built unknown, darwin/amd64)
```

**How to read it:** A release build shows a version, commit and build date. A
local `go build` shows `dev`, `none` and `unknown`, as here. `cortex --version`
prints the short form.

### `cortex completion`

**Answers:** A shell completion script for bash, zsh, fish or PowerShell.

**Use it when:** Setting up your shell.

```console
$ cortex completion zsh | head -4
#compdef cortex
compdef _cortex cortex

# zsh completion for cortex                               -*- shell-script -*-
```

**How to read it:** It is a script, not a report. Follow
`cortex completion <shell> --help` for where to save it.

### `cortex licenses`

**Answers:** Regenerates `THIRD_PARTY.md` from the Go module graph.

**Use it when:** Maintaining RepoCortex itself. It is not meant for the
repositories you index.

```console
$ cortex licenses --check      # run inside the Java sample
error: go list -m: exit status 1
```

**How to read it:** It runs `go list -m`, so it only works inside a Go module
(RepoCortex's own repository). With `--check` it exits non-zero when the
committed file is out of date, which is how CI uses it.

---

## Recipes

### 1. Onboard to a new codebase

1. `cortex init && cortex index && cortex resolve` – build the index
   ([init](#cortex-init), [index](#cortex-index), [resolve](#cortex-resolve)).
   Note the bound share in the `resolve` output.
2. `cortex languages` – check your languages are `typed` or `resolved`.
3. `cortex api` and `cortex db` – the entry points and the data.
4. `cortex infra` and `cortex events` – how it is deployed and what it
   publishes.
5. `cortex docs --out docs/generated` – a map to read, if components are
   declared; otherwise `cortex ui`.
6. `cortex missed` – where the index is blind, so you know which answers to
   double-check.

### 2. Refactor a function safely

1. `cortex callers <fn>` and `cortex references <fn>` – who depends on it.
   If the list is empty, read the bound share before believing it.
2. `cortex plan-change <fn>` – an ordered list of callers to update.
3. `cortex who <fn>` – someone to ask before you start.
4. For a rename: `cortex rename <old> <new> --floor high`, read every site and
   every leftover line, then add `--apply`.
5. After committing: `cortex index && cortex resolve`, then
   `cortex impact --base HEAD~1` to confirm the reach is what you expected.

### 3. Review a pull request

1. `cortex index && cortex resolve` on the PR branch.
2. `cortex impact --base origin/main --head HEAD` – callers at risk, and whether
   each has a test.
3. `cortex arch --crossings` – any new rule violations or new component links.
4. `cortex diff --from-index <main-index.db> --from <main-sha>` – which facts
   changed (new edges, moved endpoints, new table writers).
5. `cortex who <changed symbol>` – who else should look.

### 4. Gate CI

1. `cortex index && cortex resolve` (optionally `cortex scip import index.scip`
   from your build).
2. `cortex doctor --verify-index` – fail on a broken index.
3. `cortex --json arch --fail-on high > arch.json`
4. `cortex --json missed --fail-on high > missed.json`
5. `cortex --json impact --base origin/main --head HEAD > impact.json`
6. `cortex report pr --impact impact.json --arch arch.json --missed missed.json --out comment.md`
   and `cortex report sarif --arch arch.json --missed missed.json --out cortex.sarif`
   ([report](#cortex-report)).
7. Optional: `cortex docs --check --out docs/generated` and
   `cortex bench cases.yml --fail-on-regression`.

### 5. Give an agent context

1. `cortex agent --check` – see what is missing.
2. `cortex install --dry-run`, then `cortex install`, or run the
   `claude mcp add …` line from `cortex agent`.
3. `cortex agent --guidance >> CLAUDE.md` (or `AGENTS.md`) so the agent knows
   when to use the tools.
4. Set `mcp.profile: standard` in `.cortex.yml` if you want `impact_analysis`
   and `find_tests`; confirm with `cortex serve --list-tools`.
5. Per task: `cortex --json compile "<task>" > contract.json`, give the agent
   the contract (or let it call `get_task_context`), then check its work with
   `cortex verify --contract contract.json --changed $(git diff --name-only | paste -sd, -)`.
6. Keep the index current while it works: `cortex watch` or
   `cortex hooks install`.

# --- END FILE: docs/guides/cli-output-guide.md ---


# --- BEGIN FILE: docs/guides/portal-guide.md ---

# The RepoCortex portal: a screen-by-screen guide

`cortex ui` serves a local web portal over your RepoCortex index. It is a
reading tool. It shows what the index holds, how sure the index is about each
fact, and what the index cannot see. It never edits your code or your index.

Every screenshot in this guide is a real capture of the portal running against
the sample service in `fixtures/payment-platform` (10 files, 54 symbols, one
HTTP endpoint, two database tables). Your numbers will differ.

Contents

- [Start the portal](#start-the-portal)
- [The layout](#the-layout)
- [Reading conventions used on every screen](#reading-conventions-used-on-every-screen)
- [Screens](#screens)
  - [Index health](#index-health-soverview)
  - Understand the code: [Map of the code](#map-of-the-code-sgraph),
    [Find a symbol](#find-a-symbol-ssearch),
    [Shape of the code](#shape-of-the-code-smetrics)
  - Before you change something: [Plan a refactor](#plan-a-refactor-splanchange),
    [What could break](#what-could-break-sblast),
    [Task brief](#task-brief-scontract),
    [Check a change](#check-a-change-sverify),
    [Who knows this code](#who-knows-this-code-sownership),
    [What changed](#what-changed-sdiff)
  - How it runs: [APIs and what they touch](#apis-and-what-they-touch-scrossstack),
    [Database tables](#database-tables-stables),
    [Events and queues](#events-and-queues-sevents),
    [Settings and secrets](#settings-and-secrets-sconfig),
    [What actually ran](#what-actually-ran-strace),
    [Across repositories](#across-repositories-sestate)
  - Quality: [Test coverage](#test-coverage-stests),
    [Code blindspots](#code-blindspots-smissed),
    [Architecture rules](#architecture-rules-sgovernance),
    [Dependencies](#dependencies-sdeps),
    [How accurate is this index](#how-accurate-is-this-index-saccuracy)
  - For your AI agent: [Connect an agent](#connect-an-agent-sagent),
    [Retrieval quality](#retrieval-quality-sretrieval)
- [How the portal is designed to behave](#how-the-portal-is-designed-to-behave)
- [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting)

---

## Start the portal

The portal reads an existing index, so build one first:

```sh
cortex init
cortex index
cortex resolve
cortex ui
```

`cortex ui` prints the address and stays in the foreground. Press Ctrl-C to
stop it.

```text
RepoCortex portal: http://127.0.0.1:7777/
  index      /path/to/repo/.cortex/index.db (opened read-only; this portal never writes)
  binding    loopback only — not reachable from other machines.
```

| Flag | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--port N` | Port to listen on. Default `7777`. `0` picks a free port and prints it. |
| `--allow-refresh` | Adds a "Refresh index" button to the index bar. This is the only way the portal can write anything: it adds one POST route that rebuilds the index. Off by default. |
| `--host ADDR` | Address to bind. Default `127.0.0.1`. Anything else exposes the structure of your code to the network, and the command says so. |
| `--max-nodes N` | Most symbol nodes in one map response. Default `1500`. Anything left out is counted on screen. |
| `--print-url` | Print the address and exit without starting. |
| `--project DIR` | Serve the index of another project root (a global flag). |

What the portal guarantees:

- **Read-only.** The index is opened read-only and only GET routes exist.
  Without `--allow-refresh` no route that writes is registered at all. With
  it, a refresh still needs a header a cross-site page cannot set, and a
  request from a non-loopback origin is refused.
- **Loopback only.** It binds to `127.0.0.1` and refuses any request whose
  `Host` header is not a loopback address. A web page on the internet cannot
  use your browser to read your index.
- **Offline.** All assets are inside the `cortex` binary. There is no npm, no
  CDN, and the page's content policy blocks loading anything from another
  origin.

## The layout

![The whole Index health page at 1440 pixels wide: the rail on the left, the index bar at the top, the answer card, summary cards, runtime surface, coverage bars, blind spots and the health card, with the rail footer at the bottom](../assets/portal/layout.png)

Every screen shares the same frame:

```text
+------------------+---------------------------------------------------------------+
| RAIL             | INDEX BAR (sticky)                                            |
|  project name    |  project | index ready | indexed 2 min ago | state | sha      |
|  index path      |  [How this index was built]  [proven|very likely|uncertain|a  |
|  [Cmd-K Quick    |   guess]  [Copy link]                                         |
|   Jump]          +---------------------------------------------------------------+
|                  | ANSWER LINE                                                   |
|  Index health    |  One sentence with the key numbers in bold.                   |
|  UNDERSTAND...   |  A supporting sentence.                                       |
|   Map of the code|  Next step: [Copy: cortex <command>]  why it helps            |
|   ...            +---------------------------------------------------------------+
|  BEFORE YOU...   | CONTROLS  (input, depth, filters — only where the screen      |
|  HOW IT RUNS     |            takes a question)                                  |
|  QUALITY         +---------------------------------------------------------------+
|  FOR YOUR AI...  | SUMMARY CARDS   [ n ] [ n ] [ n ] [ n ]                       |
|                  +---------------------------------------------------------------+
|                  | TABLES AND CARDS: rows, each with a confidence word and a     |
|                  |   file:line you can copy                                      |
|                  | > Evidence — ... (fold, closed)                               |
|                  | > What this view can't see — ... (fold, closed)               |
|  FOOTER          |                                                               |
|  read-only ·     |                                                               |
|  localhost       |                                                               |
|  [What do these  |                                                               |
|   words mean?]   |                                                               |
|  [Theme: system] |                                                               |
+------------------+---------------------------------------------------------------+
```

- **Rail.** The project name, the path of the index file being read, a Quick
  Jump button, and the screens grouped by the question you are asking. Index
  health sits alone at the top because its verdict qualifies every other
  screen. Below 1000 pixels wide the rail becomes one row that scrolls
  sideways.
- **Index bar.** Sticky at the top of every screen. It shows the run verdict
  (`index ready`, or a warning colour when the run is partial, stale or has
  parse failures), the age of the index, its state, the git revision it read,
  and any parse failures. Click the verdict to jump to the freshness card on
  Index health. "How this index was built" opens a panel under the bar with
  the exact finish time, the revision, and whether a commit hook keeps the
  index current. The four confidence chips and Copy link sit on the right.
- **Answer line.** The first thing on every screen: one sentence that answers
  the screen's question, with the numbers in bold. When the server suggests a
  next step, it appears as a button that copies the command.
- **Folds.** Evidence, caveats and long lists sit in `details` folds below the
  answer. They start closed.
- **Footer.** At the bottom of the rail: the project, the run number, the
  number of files indexed, and "read-only". The "What do these words mean?"
  button opens a short glossary, and the theme button sits below it.

## Reading conventions used on every screen

### The answer line

Each screen opens with one sentence that answers its question, for example
"3 things could be affected if you change findById: 2 directly, 1 further
along the walk." No heading sits above it. If the screen needs input first, the
sentence says what to type. If the data fails to load, the sentence changes to
"<screen> could not load." and an error card below says why.

### Confidence words and colours

Every relationship carries a confidence level. The portal shows it as a word,
never as a bare id:

| Word on screen | Id in the API and CLI | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| proven (with a tick) | `exact` | a compiler proved it |
| very likely | `high` | measured 87–96% right |
| uncertain | `medium` | measured 6–38% right |
| a guess | `low` | measured under 3% right |
| unmeasured (with a `?`) | unknown | no measurement recorded |

Confidence is drawn as ink density on one neutral hue, not as a traffic-light
colour. The darker the ink, the stronger the proof. Proven is the darkest and
carries a tick. A guess is the faintest. Unmeasured uses a muted purple and a
question mark. On the map, proven and very likely edges are solid lines,
uncertain edges are dashed, and guesses are dotted. Because the levels differ
by lightness, they survive colour blindness and greyscale printing. Hover a
badge to see the measurement behind the word.

Green, amber and red are kept for status (pass, warning, failure) and never
mean confidence.

### The standard of proof

The four chips in the index bar are both the legend and a filter. Click one to
set the weakest level a screen will show; that chip and every stronger one
become pressed. The default is "uncertain and better", so guesses are hidden
until you ask for them. The choice is saved in the URL as `?floor=` and
applies to every screen. Once Index health has loaded in the tab, the chips
also show how many relationships sit at each level.

When something is hidden by this setting, the screen says how many, in its
"What this view can't see" fold.

### "What this view can't see"

Screens that list rows end with a fold named "What this view can't see". It
counts what was left out and why: rows below the chosen standard of proof,
rows past a page limit, calls that could not be bound. Each reason has a
count, and where a count is not recorded it says "how many is not recorded"
rather than showing zero. Where something can be fixed, the fold shows the
command. When nothing was left out it says so in one sentence.

Several screens also carry a fold such as "What this screen never does, and
what it cannot see". Read these before you trust an empty answer.

### Deep links and Copy link

Everything about a screen lives in the URL: the screen (`?s=blast`), the
symbol (`&sym=findById`), the depth, the standard of proof, the page, the map
view and its selection. Opening that URL in a fresh tab restores the same
screen. Copy link in the index bar copies the current URL, and the button
changes to "Link copied" for a moment.

Useful keys:

| Key | Screen | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `s` | screen id | `?s=tables` |
| `sym`, `depth` | What could break, Who knows this code, Test coverage | `?s=blast&sym=findById&depth=3` |
| `q` | Find a symbol | `?s=search&q=CallbackController` |
| `intent` | Task brief | `?s=contract&intent=Add+idempotency+to+payment+callback+processing` |
| `intent`, `changed` | Check a change | `?s=verify&intent=...&changed=src/a.java,src/b.java` |
| `csdepth`, `off`, `limit` | APIs and what they touch | `?s=crossstack&csdepth=4` |
| `dfrom`, `dto` | What changed | `?s=diff&dfrom=3&dto=4` |
| `open=1` | any | unfolds every fold (see below) |

An unknown `?s=` value falls back to Index health rather than a blank page.
Old links of the form `/#graph` still work. Back and Forward move between
screens.

### `?open=1`

Add `&open=1` to any URL and every fold on the page opens. This is meant for
screenshots, reviews and agents that read the page. It is not remembered: the
next visit without it starts with folds closed again.

### Keyboard

- Every rail entry is a real button, so Tab reaches them in order. A "Skip to
  content" link is the first stop.
- Cmd-K (Ctrl-K on Windows and Linux) opens Quick Jump, a palette for going to
  any screen by name. Esc closes it.
- On Map of the code, `/` jumps to the search box from anywhere on the screen.
  With the canvas focused: arrow keys pan (hold Shift to move further), `+`
  and `-` zoom, `0` fits the drawing, Tab and Shift-Tab walk the nodes, and
  Enter opens the selected node.
- Search boxes with suggestions accept Up, Down, Enter and Esc.

### Theme

The theme button in the rail footer cycles Theme: system, Theme: light,
Theme: dark. The choice is kept in your browser and survives a reload. "system"
follows your operating system's setting.

### The glossary

"What do these words mean?" opens one-sentence definitions of the few terms
the portal cannot avoid: index, symbol, relationship, package, endpoint, hop,
lower bound, degraded, blast radius and compiler-backed. The same definitions
appear when you hover those words where they are underlined.

---

## Screens

The same template is used for each screen. "Data comes from" names the API
route the screen calls (all are GET, on the same port) and the CLI command
that gives the same answer in a terminal.

### Index health (`?s=overview`)

**Answers:** How fresh and how complete is this index, and where is it blind?
**Data comes from:** `/api/overview` (with `/api/indexstate` for the build
panel). CLI: `cortex status` and `cortex doctor`.

![Index health: answer line saying the index was built seconds ago and every file was read, a Copy cortex watch button, a summary banner, three entry cards, and counts for files, relationships, directories and exported symbols](../assets/portal/overview.png)

**Layout skeleton:**

```text
[ANSWER  Indexed 27 seconds ago. Every file was read.  [Copy: cortex watch]]
[System banner: inbound APIs -> services -> repositories -> tables]
[Entry cards: architecture | change safety | agents]
[FILES] [RELATIONSHIPS] [DIRECTORIES] [EXPORTED SURFACE]
[Runtime surface: endpoints, tables, next step]
[API list]                [Table list]
[What are you about to change?  (task box -> Task brief)]
[Resolution coverage: bound | unresolved | ambiguous | compiler-proven + bars]
> Evidence — how sure each relationship is
[Blind spots: language x edge kind with symbols but no edges]
[Index health and freshness: verdict | age | files indexed | parse failures]
> What this view can't see
```

**How to read it:**

- **Answer line.** Good: "Every file was read." Worrying: a partial run, parse
  failures, or an age over a day. The button under it is the next step the
  server suggests: `cortex watch` when all is well, `cortex index` when the
  index is partial or stale.
- **Summary cards.** Files, relationships, directories (or components, if you
  declared an architecture) and exported symbols. These are the totals every
  other screen counts against.
- **Runtime surface.** Endpoints and tables the index found, with links to
  APIs and what they touch and Database tables.
- **What are you about to change?** Type a task and press Compile to go
  straight to a Task brief.
- **Resolution coverage.** How many references were bound to exactly one
  definition, how many were ambiguous, how many stayed unbound, and how many
  are compiler-proven. A low bound share means every answer on every screen
  is a lower bound. The note under the bars says which command raises it.
- **Blind spots.** Each row is a language and a relationship kind that has
  symbols but zero edges. That is a gap in what the index can see, not proof
  that your code has no such relationships. Read this before trusting an
  empty answer elsewhere.
- **Index health and freshness.** The verdict (`ready`, or a warning), age,
  files indexed against files discovered, and parse failures.
- **Where to go next:** Map of the code for structure, What could break before
  a change, How accurate is this index if most edges are unmeasured.

### Map of the code (`?s=graph`)

**Answers:** Which parts of the code talk to each other, and how sure is each
link?
**Data comes from:** `/api/graph` (and `/api/source` for the Code view). CLI:
`cortex export --format svg|json|dot|graphml|csv`.

![Map of the code: answer line saying 10 directories talk to each other through 6 relationships, view tabs Graph, Tree, Treemap and Code, scope and detail controls, and a layered drawing of directory boxes joined by arrows](../assets/portal/graph.png)

**Layout skeleton:**

```text
[ANSWER  10 directories talk to each other: 6 relationships ...]
[Breadcrumb: Repository]                 [Graph | Tree | Treemap | Code]
[SCOPE ...] [DETAIL LEVEL ...] [FIND ... press /] [Filters]
+--------------------------------------------------------------+
| [Grouped] Layout [Layered v] [+] [-] 124% [Fit] [minimap]    |
|   boxes = groups, arrows = relationships, line style = proof |
+--------------------------------------------------------------+
[Scope banner: what was chosen and why]
[Every relationship on the map, with its evidence  (table)]
> What this view can't see
```

**How to read it:**

- **Answer line.** How many groups and relationships are drawn, and whether
  the map shows all of them.
- **View tabs.** Graph is the drawing. Tree lists what is inside each group.
  Treemap sizes groups by a measure you choose. Code shows a file with line
  numbers. All four share the same address, so a link keeps the view.
- **Toolbar.** Scope narrows to one group. Detail level goes from the whole
  system down to directories, files and symbols. Find (or `/`) searches the
  drawn names. Filters holds grouping, language, edge kinds, the standard of
  proof and focus depth; the button shows how many are changed from the
  default, so a narrowed map never looks like the whole one.
- **Canvas.** Click a box to select it, open it to go a level deeper. Line
  style tells you the confidence of each edge (solid, dashed, dotted). A
  number on a box is how many relationships it has.
- **Scope banner.** If you did not choose a scope, it says which one was
  chosen and by what rule, instead of drawing an empty canvas.
- **Relationship table.** A full text version of the drawing. Each row has
  the weakest confidence along it and an example file and line. This table is
  the thing to cite in a review.
- **Where to go next:** Shape of the code for the riskiest symbols, What could
  break for one symbol.

### Find a symbol (`?s=search`)

**Answers:** Is this name in the index at all, and where is it defined?
**Data comes from:** `/api/symbols`. CLI: `cortex symbol <name>` (exact
match) or `cortex search <text>` (full text).

![Find a symbol: answer line saying 8 definitions are named CallbackController, a search box, counts for matches, shown and exported, and a table of definitions with kind, match type, edges, confidence and a Blast radius button per row](../assets/portal/search.png)

**Layout skeleton:**

```text
[ANSWER  8 definitions named CallbackController.]
[SYMBOL NAME ______________________________] [Search]
[MATCHES] [SHOWN] [EXPORTED]
[Definitions: symbol + fqn | kind | match | edges | extraction | file | [Blast radius]]
```

**How to read it:**

- **Answer line.** How many definitions carry that name. Zero here is the
  real "not in the index" answer that every empty result elsewhere depends on.
- **Match column.** `exact`, `prefix` or `contains`. Results are ranked with
  exact matches first.
- **Edges.** How many relationships touch the definition. Zero edges on a
  class you know is used points to a blind spot (see Index health).
- **Extraction.** The confidence word for how the definition was read.
- **Blast radius button.** Opens What could break for that exact definition,
  which avoids the "this name matches several things" step.

### Shape of the code (`?s=metrics`)

**Answers:** Which symbols are most connected, so a change there is most
dangerous, and are there cycles?
**Data comes from:** `/api/metrics`. CLI: `cortex export` (the full ranking
under the same keys).

![Shape of the code: answer line naming the 5 most connected symbols and 0 cycles, level and filter controls, and a ranked table with score, fan-in, fan-out, instability and location](../assets/portal/metrics.png)

**Layout skeleton:**

```text
[ANSWER  The 5 most connected symbols ... and the 0 cycles between them.  [Copy: cortex export]]
[LEVEL symbol v]  [FILTERS: callable kinds only | exclude test files]
(note: level, standard of proof, filters applied)
[Where change is dangerous: rank | what | kind | score | fan-in | fan-out | instability | where]
[... further measures ...]
> What this view can't see
```

**How to read it:**

- **Level and filters.** Rank symbols, files or groups. "callable kinds only"
  drops fields and types; "exclude test files" drops test code. The note
  under the controls states exactly what was applied.
- **Where change is dangerous.** Ranked by betweenness: how many shortest paths
  run through a symbol. It measures position, not importance, and it is
  sampled, so ranks near the cut-off can differ from a full computation.
- **Fan-in, fan-out, instability.** High fan-in means many callers depend on
  it. Instability near 1 means it depends on much and little depends on it.
- **Where to go next:** click through to What could break for the top rows.

### Plan a refactor (`?s=planchange`)

**Answers:** In what order should a change to this symbol be made, and what
must hold before and after?
**Data comes from:** `/api/planchange`. CLI: `cortex plan-change <symbol>`.

![Plan a refactor: a symbol box containing findById, a summary card with its file and a moderate risk score, and numbered steps to modify the method and update its two direct callers](../assets/portal/planchange.png)

**Layout skeleton:**

```text
[ANSWER  Deterministic refactoring planner: ...]
[symbol ____________________] [Generate Blueprint]
 example chips
[Target: name, file:line            Risk score, direct and total callers]
Execution Blueprint (ordered steps)
 (1) Modify the target ...
 (2) Update direct caller ...
[Preconditions]        [Postconditions]
```

**How to read it:**

- Type a symbol name and press Generate Blueprint. If the name matches several
  definitions you get a list to pick from.
- **Target card.** The definition that was planned, with a risk score and how
  many callers it has.
- **Steps.** Change the target first, then each caller, in dependency order.
- **Preconditions and postconditions.** What should be true before you start
  and which tests should pass after.
- This screen does not read `?sym=` from the URL, so a link cannot reopen a
  plan; use the CLI command for something you can share.

### What could break (`?s=blast`)

**Answers:** If I change this symbol, what else could be affected?
**Data comes from:** `/api/blast`. CLI: `cortex callers <name>` gives the
first step; the full walk is the MCP tool `impact_analysis`.

![What could break for findById: answer line saying 3 things could be affected, 2 directly and 1 further along, with moderate risk; the target card; counts for direct, indirect, covering tests and risk](../assets/portal/blast.png)

**Layout skeleton:**

```text
[ANSWER  3 things could be affected if you change findById: 2 directly, 1 further ...]
[SYMBOL ______________________] [DEPTH 3 v] [Analyse]
[Target: name, confidence, fqn, file:line]
[DIRECT] [INDIRECT] [COVERING TESTS] [RISK]
> Evidence — why the risk is <level>, in N factors
[The files a change lands in]
[What it reaches: symbol | depth | via | confidence | file]
[What it touches outside the code: tables read/written, endpoints exposed]
[Tests that cover it]
[What this walk could not see]
> This answer is a lower bound — N caveats
```

**How to read it:**

- **No symbol yet.** The screen explains why a bare name may not be enough and
  waits for input.
- **Ambiguous name.** You get a list of candidates, each with an "Analyse this
  one" button. Use the fully qualified form (`path/File.java:Name`) to skip
  this.
- **Counts.** Direct is one hop away. Indirect is further along, up to the
  chosen depth. Every reached symbol carries the confidence of the weakest
  link on the path that found it.
- **Risk.** Low, moderate or high with a score out of 100. Open the Evidence
  fold to see the factors behind it.
- **Tests that cover it.** Proven tests and tests that only share a name are
  shown apart. A test matched by name alone is marked uncertain.
- **What this walk could not see.** Unbound calls and depth limits. A result of
  zero with caveats here is a lower bound, not a guarantee.
- **Where to go next:** Who knows this code to find a reviewer, Task brief to
  scope the work.

### Task brief (`?s=contract`)

**Answers:** For this task, what is in scope, what is not, and what could the
index not find out?
**Data comes from:** `/api/contract`. CLI: `cortex compile "<task>"` (add
`--json` to save the contract for Check a change).

![Task brief for "Add idempotency to payment callback processing": answer line with 9 entries in scope, 0 covering tests and 6 unknowns, a task box with a scope budget, count cards, and the "What was asked, and what was understood" card](../assets/portal/contract.png)

**Layout skeleton:**

```text
[ANSWER  A brief for "<task>": 9 entries in scope, 0 tests ..., 6 things it could not find out.
         [Answer the 6 unknowns before starting]]
[TASK ______________________________] [SCOPE BUDGET 12 v] [Compile]
[IN SCOPE] [EXPLICITLY NOT] [REACHED] [UNKNOWNS]
[What was asked, and what was understood]
[What the index cannot answer]   (open by default, listed first)
> Evidence — scope, non-scope, constraints, tests ...
[Open -> Check a change]
```

**How to read it:**

- **Unknowns come first.** Each one is a question the index could not answer.
  An agent given this brief would have to guess them, so answer them before
  starting.
- **What was understood.** The concepts and anchor symbols the task was matched
  to. If these are wrong, reword the task.
- **In scope and explicitly not.** What the change should touch, and nearby
  code it should leave alone. Scope budget caps the in-scope list.
- **Where to go next:** "Open" carries the same task to Check a change.

### Check a change (`?s=verify`)

**Answers:** Did a finished change stay inside its brief and break nothing
the index can see?
**Data comes from:** `/api/verify`. CLI:
`cortex verify --contract contract.json --changed <files>`.

![Check a change: answer line reading Pass with 0 things broken and 0 that might be, task and changed-files boxes, a green PASS banner, and counts for changed files, in scope, undeclared and facts](../assets/portal/verify.png)

**Layout skeleton:**

```text
[ANSWER  Pass: 0 things this change broke, 0 it might have.  [Copy: cortex verify ...]]
[TASK THE CHANGE WAS COMPILED FROM ____] [CHANGED FILES ____] [Verify]
[PASS | ADVISORY | UNVERIFIED banner, exit code]
[CHANGED FILES] [IN SCOPE] [UNDECLARED] [FACTS]
> Evidence — the questions this check asked
[Findings]
> Evidence — every changed file
```

**How to read it:**

- Paste the task and a comma-separated list of changed files (for example from
  `git diff --name-only | paste -sd, -`). Nothing is written and no git command
  is run.
- **Banner.** Pass, advisory or unverified are shown in different styles. The
  exit code is what the same check returns in CI.
- **Undeclared.** Files the change touched that the brief took no position on.
  More than zero means the change went outside its scope.
- **Findings.** Each finding says whether a compiler proved it or a name
  suggested it.

### Who knows this code (`?s=ownership`)

**Answers:** Who has touched the code that a change to this symbol can reach?
**Data comes from:** `/api/who`. CLI: `cortex who <symbol>`.

![Who knows this code for findById: answer line saying 1 person has touched the reachable code, counts for symbols reached, attributable, files reached and people found, and a ranking table](../assets/portal/ownership.png)

**Layout skeleton:**

```text
[ANSWER  1 person has touched the code a change to findById can reach.]
[SYMBOL ____] [DEPTH v]
[Routing a review of findById]
[SYMBOLS REACHED] [ATTRIBUTABLE] [FILES REACHED] [PEOPLE FOUND]
[Who has context: person | share | symbols | files | commits | last touch | basis]
[Bus factor over the reached files]
> Evidence — the reached set
> The window of history this was read over
[What a name in this ranking does and does not mean]
```

**How to read it:**

- The ranking is over the same set What could break would reach, then read
  from git history.
- **Bus factor.** Files that only one person touched. Many rows here mean
  review knowledge is thin.
- A name in the ranking means that person changed those files in the history
  window. It does not mean they own or understand the code.

### What changed (`?s=diff`)

**Answers:** Which facts about the code changed between two indexed runs?
**Data comes from:** `/api/diff`. CLI: `cortex diff`.

![What changed: answer line saying the index holds only one run so there is nothing to compare, a Copy cortex index button, and base and head run boxes with not-compared counts](../assets/portal/diff.png)

**Layout skeleton:**

```text
[ANSWER  This index holds only one run, so there is nothing to compare.  [Copy: cortex index]]
[BASE RUN ____] [HEAD RUN ____] [Compare]
[RELATIONSHIPS GAINED] [LOST] [RE-GRADED DOWNWARDS] [COVERING TESTS LOST]
[why there is nothing to compare / the diff rows]
```

**How to read it:**

- One index file normally holds one committed run, so this screen is usually
  empty. That is the normal state, not a fault. To compare across commits, run
  `cortex diff --from-index <other index.db> ...` in a terminal.
- With two runs, watch "lost" and "re-graded downwards": a relationship that
  got weaker or a test that stopped covering code.
- The run ids go in the URL as `dfrom` and `dto`. (The empty-state text
  mentions `?from=`/`?to=`; those are the API's own parameter names.)

### APIs and what they touch (`?s=crossstack`)

**Answers:** For each endpoint, which handler serves it and which database
tables it reaches?
**Data comes from:** `/api/crossstack`. CLI: `cortex api`.

![APIs and what they touch: answer line saying 1 endpoint reaches a database table, walk depth and page controls, counts for routes, with a handler, with a caller and reaching a table, and a table explaining where chains stop](../assets/portal/crossstack.png)

**Layout skeleton:**

```text
[ANSWER  1 endpoint. On this page, 1 of 1 reach a database table.  [next step]]
[HANDLER WALK DEPTH v] [ROUTES PER PAGE v] [< Prev] routes 1-1 of 1 [Next >]
[ROUTES] [WITH A HANDLER] [WITH A CALLER] [REACHING A TABLE]
[Where the chains stop, and why: stage | reason | chains | what it means]
[Chains: client -> endpoint -> handler -> service -> table, drawn at the weakest hop]
```

**How to read it:**

- Each chain runs client, endpoint, handler, service, table, and is shown at
  the confidence of its weakest step.
- **With a caller = 0.** Either the routes are called from outside this
  repository (a public API) or client calls were never extracted. The
  overview's blind spots tell these apart.
- **Where the chains stop.** Every chain that ended early says where and why,
  with a remedy such as raising the walk depth.
- Counts on the cards are for the chains on this page; paging moves through
  the rest.

### Database tables (`?s=tables`)

**Answers:** Which tables does this code use, and who writes and reads each?
**Data comes from:** `/api/db`. CLI: `cortex db` and `cortex db table <name>`.

![Database tables: answer line saying 2 tables, 2 written and 1 read by the code, count cards, and a table of every table with read and write statement counts](../assets/portal/tables.png)

**Layout skeleton:**

```text
[ANSWER  2 tables. 2 are written by this code, 1 is read by it.]
[TABLES] [WITH A RECORDED WRITER] [WITH A RECORDED READER] [NO RECORDED ACCESSOR]
> What a static SQL read cannot see
[Every table: table | standing | read stmts | write stmts | uncertain | readers | writers | declared at]
[Who writes, and who only reads — per table: written by / read by, with confidence and evidence]
```

**How to read it:**

- A table with writers but no readers, or no accessor at all, is worth a look:
  it may be read by another service, or by SQL this index cannot parse.
- Open "What a static SQL read cannot see" before concluding a table is unused.
  Dynamic SQL and ORM-generated queries can be invisible.

### Events and queues (`?s=events`)

**Answers:** Which message topics does this code publish to or consume from?
**Data comes from:** `/api/events`. CLI: `cortex events`.

![Events and queues: answer line saying 0 topics, 0 publishers and 0 consumers, and an empty-state card naming the supported brokers](../assets/portal/events.png)

**Layout skeleton:**

```text
[ANSWER  0 topics across Kafka, RabbitMQ, SQS, SNS, and Pub/Sub. 0 publishers, 0 consumers.]
[topic list: topic | publishers | consumers]   or   [empty-state card]
```

**How to read it:**

- The sample service uses no message broker, so this screen is empty. The card
  lists the client libraries that are recognised.
- A topic with publishers but no consumers (or the reverse) in one repository
  is normal when the other side lives elsewhere; check Across repositories.

### Settings and secrets (`?s=config`)

**Answers:** Which configuration keys exist, which are read, and which look
sensitive?
**Data comes from:** `/api/config`. CLI: `cortex config`.

![Settings and secrets: answer line saying no setting is recorded and the reason is stated below, a Copy cortex config button, and counts for keys, read but declared nowhere, declared but never read, and sensitive by name](../assets/portal/config.png)

**Layout skeleton:**

```text
[ANSWER  No setting is recorded in this index, and the reason is stated below.  [Copy: cortex config]]
[KEYS] [READ, DECLARED NOWHERE] [DECLARED, NEVER READ] [SENSITIVE BY NAME]
[keys table]  or  [why this index recorded no configuration]
> What this screen never does, and what it cannot see
```

**How to read it:**

- No value is ever read. A key is marked sensitive by its name alone.
- **Read, declared nowhere.** The most urgent column: a service that needs
  these keys and does not find them fails at start-up.
- **Declared, never read.** Dead configuration, or a lookup this scan cannot
  see.
- Kubernetes, Helm, Terraform and CI definitions are not read. An empty screen
  means nothing recognisable was found, not that the service has no settings.

### What actually ran (`?s=trace`)

**Answers:** Which endpoints and code paths were exercised in a real trace?
**Data comes from:** `/api/trace`. CLI: `cortex trace cortex.trace.json`.

![What actually ran: answer line saying no trace export was placed at cortex.trace.json, a Copy command button, and counts for spans, indexed endpoints, indexed symbols and exercised entities](../assets/portal/trace.png)

**Layout skeleton:**

```text
[ANSWER  No trace export has been placed at cortex.trace.json.  [Copy: cortex trace ...]]
[SPANS] [INDEXED ENDPOINTS] [INDEXED SYMBOLS] [EXERCISED ENTITIES]
[The file this screen reads: where it looked]
[hot / cold endpoints]  or  [why there is nothing to lay over the graph]
```

**How to read it:**

- Export an OpenTelemetry (OTLP/JSON) or Jaeger trace and save it as
  `cortex.trace.json` in the repository root, or pass `?export=<path>`.
- Without a trace, endpoints are "unobserved", which is different from "cold".
  The screen will not call code dead because no trace was given.

### Across repositories (`?s=estate`)

**Answers:** How does this repository connect to the other repositories in the
system?
**Data comes from:** `/api/system`. CLI: `cortex system --members cortex.system.yml`.

![Across repositories: answer line saying there is no estate manifest at cortex.system.yml, a Copy command button, and counts for members declared, cross-repository calls, shared tables and completeness](../assets/portal/estate.png)

**Layout skeleton:**

```text
[ANSWER  No estate manifest at cortex.system.yml.  [Copy: cortex system --members ...]]
[MEMBERS DECLARED] [CROSS-REPOSITORY CALLS] [SHARED TABLES] [COMPLETE]
[The file this screen reads]
[members, cross-repo calls, shared tables]  or  [why it is empty]
```

**How to read it:**

- Which repositories make up your system is not something one index can
  know, so you list them in a committed `cortex.system.yml` (or pass
  `?estate=<path>`).
- Once declared, each cross-repository call has a confidence word and a file
  and line on both ends. Shared tables written by more than one member are
  worth a review.

### Test coverage (`?s=tests`)

**Answers:** Which symbols does a test provably reach?
**Data comes from:** `/api/tests`. There is no separate CLI command in this
build; the MCP tool `find_tests` gives the same answer for one symbol.

![Test coverage: answer line saying 0 of 48 symbols have a test that reaches them through a recorded relationship, a Copy cortex resolve button, a symbol box and depth, and count cards](../assets/portal/tests.png)

**Layout skeleton:**

```text
[ANSWER  0 of 48 symbols have a test that reaches them ...  [Copy: cortex resolve]]
[COVERAGE FOR ONE SYMBOL (optional) ____] [TRAVERSAL DEPTH v]
[TEST FILES] [NON-TEST SYMBOLS] [WITH A PROVEN COVERING TEST] [WITH NO PROVEN COVERING TEST]
> What each of the 3 verdicts means
[explanation card when nothing is proven]
> What the two lists below are, and are not
> Evidence — every test file
[Symbols a test reaches through a recorded edge]
[Tests suggested by a naming convention only]
```

**How to read it:**

- "Proven" coverage means a test reaches the symbol through a recorded
  relationship. A test that only shares a name (for example
  `CallbackControllerTest`) is listed separately and never counted as proven.
- **With no proven covering test.** This is an absence of proof, not proof of
  no test. On the sample service every symbol lands here because Java test
  calls are not bound to their targets without a compiler-backed index.
- Enter a symbol to see the tests for that one symbol.

### Code blindspots (`?s=missed`)

**Answers:** Where can the index see code but not prove anything about it?
**Data comes from:** `/api/missed`. CLI: `cortex missed`.

![Code blindspots: answer line saying 37 blindspots were found, count cards for unresolved calls, untested critical symbols, unmapped endpoints and orphan tables, and a findings table with severity, category, target, location and remediation](../assets/portal/missed.png)

**Layout skeleton:**

```text
[ANSWER  37 blindspots identified across ...]
[UNRESOLVED CALLS] [UNTESTED CRITICAL] [UNMAPPED ENDPOINTS] [ORPHAN TABLES]
[Prioritized findings: severity | category | target | location | remediation]
```

**How to read it:**

- **Unresolved calls.** Calls that could not be bound to a definition, often
  library calls. Many of these lower the confidence of every walk.
- **Untested critical, unmapped endpoints, orphan tables.** Exported code with
  no proven test, routes with no handler, and tables nothing reads or writes.
- Each row has a file and line you can copy, and a suggested fix.

### Architecture rules (`?s=governance`)

**Answers:** Does the code cross any line the declared architecture forbids?
**Data comes from:** `/api/governance`. CLI: `cortex arch` (add
`--fail-on <severity>` in CI).

![Architecture rules: answer line saying no architecture is declared so there is nothing to check, a Copy cortex arch --help button, and a standard-of-proof selector](../assets/portal/governance.png)

**Layout skeleton:**

```text
[ANSWER  No architecture is declared, so there is nothing to check ...  [Copy: cortex arch --help]]
[STANDARD OF PROOF FOR A VIOLATION v]
[violations table]  or  [No architecture is declared for this repository]
```

**How to read it:**

- Declare components and rules in `.cortex.yml`. Until then the map groups by
  directory and no rule can be broken. That is different from "no
  violations".
- Once rules exist, each violation has a confidence word. Choose the standard
  of proof that should count as a real violation in your CI gate.

### Dependencies (`?s=deps`)

**Answers:** What does this repository declare it depends on, and does anything
import each one?
**Data comes from:** `/api/deps`. CLI: `cortex deps`.

![Dependencies: answer line saying no dependency manifest was read and the reason is stated below, and counts for declared, declared but imported by nothing, declared and imported, and imported but declared nowhere](../assets/portal/deps.png)

**Layout skeleton:**

```text
[ANSWER  No dependency manifest was read ...  [Copy: cortex deps]]
[DECLARED] [DECLARED, IMPORTED BY NOTHING] [DECLARED AND IMPORTED] [IMPORTED, DECLARED NOWHERE]
[dependency table]  or  [why this screen has no manifest to read]
[language tiers]
```

**How to read it:**

- Manifests read: `go.mod`, `package.json`, `pom.xml`, `build.gradle`,
  `requirements.txt`, `pyproject.toml`, `Cargo.toml`. Lock files are not read.
- **Declared, imported by nothing** is a prompt to check, never a verdict that
  a dependency is unused.
- **Imported, declared nowhere** lists import paths that match no declaration.

### How accurate is this index (`?s=accuracy`)

**Answers:** How often are this index's relationships right, measured against
a compiler?
**Data comes from:** `/api/accuracy`. CLI: `cortex accuracy`.

![How accurate is this index: answer line saying accuracy is not measured yet and a compiler-backed index must be imported first, a Copy cortex scip import button, and precision, recall and F1 cards all reading not measured](../assets/portal/accuracy.png)

**Layout skeleton:**

```text
[ANSWER  Not measured yet: import a compiler-backed index first ...  [Copy: cortex scip import index.scip]]
[PRECISION] [RECALL] [F1] [COMPILER FACTS IN THIS INDEX]
[why recall was not measured]
> how the rates are computed
```

**How to read it:**

- Until a compiler (SCIP) index is imported, every rate reads "not measured".
  The screen never prints zero for a rate nothing has checked.
- After import, precision says how many of the index's relationships the
  compiler agrees with; recall says how many of the compiler's it found.

### Connect an agent (`?s=agent`)

**Answers:** How do I connect an AI coding agent to this index over MCP?
**Data comes from:** `/api/agent`. CLI: `cortex agent` (prints the
registration) and `cortex install` (registers with detected agents).

![Connect an agent: answer line with the symbols, relationships, files and tools the index offers, count cards for MCP tools, symbols and indexed surface, and configuration snippets for two agent clients](../assets/portal/agent.png)

**Layout skeleton:**

```text
[ANSWER  An agent ... can ask about <N> symbols and <N> relationships ... through <N> tools.  [Copy: cortex install --rules]]
[MCP TOOLS] [SYMBOLS] [INDEXED SURFACE]
[Connect via MCP:  client 1 config JSON [Copy]   client 2 config JSON [Copy]]
[sample file before and after pruning, when a readable file exists]
[MCP tools: name, category, what it does]
[What this pillar answers] [Why this screen is empty for this index]
```

**How to read it:**

- The counts are read from the index. The screen does not estimate token
  savings; the only token figures are on the sample file, measured by pruning
  a real file from this repository.
- Copy the configuration block for your agent client into its MCP settings
  file. It runs `cortex --project <repo> serve`, the same entry
  `cortex install` writes.
- The tool list is the server's own: the default `minimal` profile exposes the
  first seven tools, `standard` all 18.
- The guidance cards at the end explain why the portal cannot show an agent
  conversation: the MCP server is a separate process the portal is not part of.

### Retrieval quality (`?s=retrieval`)

**Answers:** Does the context engine hand an agent the right code for a task?
**Data comes from:** `/api/bench`. CLI: `cortex bench cortex.bench.yml`.

![Retrieval quality: answer line saying there is no benchmark case file at cortex.bench.yml, a Copy cortex bench button, and cards for cases, mean recall, mean forbid score and cases with no forbid list](../assets/portal/retrieval.png)

**Layout skeleton:**

```text
[ANSWER  No benchmark case file at cortex.bench.yml.  [Copy: cortex bench cortex.bench.yml]]
[CASES] [MEAN RECALL] [MEAN FORBID SCORE] [CASES WITH NO FORBID LIST]
```
